content.user_title: Build Azure Cosmos DB TypeScript Apps
content.value_statement: Cosmos DB SDK details can slow TypeScript development. This skill gives focused examples for authentication, CRUD, queries, bulk operations, partition keys, errors, and service layers.
actual_capabilities: Shows @azure/cosmos installation and Node.js version guidance.
Explains DefaultAzureCredential and key-based client setup.
Provides typed CRUD, patch, upsert, and delete examples.
Covers parameterized queries, pagination, and cross-partition reads.
Demonstrates bulk operations, ETag concurrency, and service layers.
Lists important SDK types and related Azure packages.
limitations: Covers the data-plane SDK, not ARM account provisioning.
Does not replace Azure security or cost reviews.
Examples require valid Azure credentials and Cosmos DB resources.
Version details may need checking against current package releases.

use_cases.title: Create Typed Data Access
use_cases.description: Build CRUD methods for documents with partition keys, typed responses, and clear error handling.

use_cases.title: Improve Query Workflows
use_cases.description: Design parameterized queries with pagination, continuation tokens, and partition-aware access patterns.

use_cases.title: Review Cosmos SDK Usage
use_cases.description: Check service-layer code for authentication choices, bulk writes, ETags, and 429 handling.

prompt_templates.title: Connect Safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to connect a TypeScript app to Cosmos DB with DefaultAzureCredential and required environment variables.

prompt_templates.title: Build CRUD Methods
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a CRUD example for a Product document using partition key category and typed @azure/cosmos responses.

prompt_templates.title: Design Queries
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a parameterized query workflow with pagination, continuation tokens, and 429 retry handling for a container.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Service Layer
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Cosmos DB service layer for partition key use, ETag concurrency, bulk writes, and authentication risks.

output_examples.input: I need a Cosmos DB product service in TypeScript.
output_examples.output: A service outline with client setup, typed CRUD methods, partition key usage, and error handling notes.

output_examples.input: I need safer query patterns for user filters.
output_examples.output: A query plan using parameters, page limits, continuation tokens, and guidance to avoid broad cross-partition scans.

output_examples.input: I need to update many documents efficiently.
output_examples.output: A bulk operation approach with operation types, partition key planning, result checks, and retry considerations.

best_practices: Prefer DefaultAzureCredential instead of long-lived account keys.
Use parameterized queries for user-controlled values.
Always model and pass the correct partition key.
anti_patterns: Do not use string concatenation for query filters.
Do not rely on cross-partition queries for routine lookups.
Do not log account keys, connection strings, or document secrets.

faq.question: Does this skill create Azure Cosmos DB accounts?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on data-plane operations with @azure/cosmos.

faq.question: Can it help with TypeScript types?
faq.answer: Yes. It lists common SDK types and shows typed document operations.

faq.question: Does it support Azure AD authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends DefaultAzureCredential for client authentication.

faq.question: Does it cover key-based authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows key and connection string setup as secondary options.

faq.question: Can it help with bulk writes?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains bulk operation inputs and result checks.

faq.question: Does it include security guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends parameterized queries, Azure AD authentication, and secret-safe configuration.
